content:
aj: quick handoff — I'm logging off at 16:30 PT. leaving a short APAC gap tonight (22:00–02:00 UTC). primary: maya (US‑EAST), secondary: kevin (EU). if anything P1/P2 hits during the gap please follow the escalation steps below.

maya: acked. I'll be primary for the window, reachable on pager and Slack. planning to stay online until 22:30 UTC.

kevin: ack — i'll take secondary. if i'm slow to respond ping me on mobile @kevin.

aj: paste of high-level checklist i'm leaving: 
- confirm primary/secondary reachable
- leave links to runbooks and active incidents
- note any risk windows or deploys

aj: runbooks: <https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/model-serving|Model Serving Runbook> and <https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/gpu-pool|GPU Pool Recovery>. key snippets below.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: aj -> maya (primary) / kevin (secondary). coverage window: 2026-03-14T22:00:00Z to 2026-03-15T02:00:00Z.

aj: escalation policy (short):
1) Page primary (maya) via PagerDuty for P1/P2. wait 5 minutes for acknowledgement.
2) If no ack or unresolved after 10 minutes, escalate to secondary (kevin).
3) If still unresolved after 20 minutes or if severity increases (customer data loss / broad outage), page ENG-L1 (team leads) and the SRE oncall.
4) For safety: immediate page to infra-sre and Eng Director for SEV0/data-loss.

aj: paging examples (pagerduty CLI):
```
pd incident create --service Model-Serving --urgency high --title "P1: model-serving high latency" --user aj
pd incident notify --incident INC12345 --channel pager
```

maya: small clarification — for noisy latency blips (<10% traffic, <3 min) please post here and tag me before paging PD unless it crosses the P1 thresholds in the runbook.

kevin: if it ends up being GPU OOMs or a single-node hotspot, try rolling instances first, see snippet: 
```
# drain node gracefully
kubectl cordon gpu-node-3
kubectl drain gpu-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# restart serving pod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving
```

aj: note on customer impact assessment: ask these three quick Qs when triaging: 
- how many customers affected (estimate)
- is data being lost or just degraded latency?
- is there a safe fallback (smaller model, cached responses) we can flip?

maya: understood. i'll use the incident template and post an initial impact summary in this thread if something pops.

sophie: FYI — we have a low-risk canary deploy at 03:00 UTC to the dedicated pool. that falls inside the coverage window; please mark it in the runbook and if you see failures revert and follow the deploy rollback steps.

aj: deploy rollback quick command (for canaries):
```
# revert to previous revision
kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=42
```

incident-bot: Alert: model-serving latency spike detected (p90 > 2.5s) — 1910012350. auto-notify disabled for APAC gap.

maya: i'm taking a look at the alert now — will post findings in 5.

kevin: ping me if you need me to stand up a spare GPU pool or toggle fallback routes.

maya: quick triage update — spike is concentrated on a single pod set, traffic routing imbalance suspected. trying a controlled restart now.

maya: restart done, tailing logs. latency returning to normal for now, continuing to monitor.

aj: super — thanks all. leaving my phone in case of escalation.

ops-rotations: reminder: do not escalate to infra-sre for transient blips under 5 minutes unless CPU/GPU errors or data loss are observed. follow the timed escalation above.

kevin: good catch. i'll stay on standby until 23:00 UTC.

maya: closing the loop — stable at 00:15 UTC, no further action needed. i'll update the post-incident note if anything reappears.

aj: thanks team, enjoy the rest of your shifts. :party-parrot:
